## Getting started

``` python
from pathlib import Path
from vishalakshi.skill import vault
v = vault()                      # $VISHALAKSHI_VAULT, else ~/.vishalakshi/vault.db
v.add(Path('~/notes').expanduser())   # a directory, a file, or text; `~` is not expanded for you
v.grab('1706.03762')             # an arXiv id, YouTube link, GitHub repo, PDF link or path
v.note('what I concluded', tags=['retrieval'])
v.note('what I concluded', title='late chunking', key='late-chunking')   # same key: one document, replaced
```

Adding a source again re-reads it only when its content changed, and the
result’s `changed` says whether it did.

## Reading it back

``` python
v.context(q)                     # whole sections plus what they connect to; hand this to a model
v.ask(q)                         # answer with [n] citations -> node_ids
v.search(q, limit=10)            # chunk hits
v.sections(q, limit=5)           # ranked sections
v.read(node_id)                  # section behind a citation
```

`kind=` filters by how a document arrived: `v.search(q, kind='pdf')`, or
several as `'note,web'`. The kinds are `web`, `pdf`, `arxiv`, `youtube`,
`file`, `code`, `data`, `note` and `image`. Every row carries `age`
(seconds since it was filed) and `stale`, and stale rows sort last.
`v.mark_stale(ref, reason=)` sets the mark, and adding the document
again with new content clears it.

## Named documents

``` python
v.ask_doc(['a.py', 'b.py'], 'what does a do that b does not?')
v.ask_doc(path, 'what is owed and by when?', schema='amount:float, due:str')
```

A path on disk is read even when it is not in the vault yet. The named
documents share one character budget, `doc_chars`.

## Paperwork

``` python
v.categorize(ref, llm='never')   # cue table first; a model only when the cues cannot decide
v.extract(ref)                   # doctype picks the schema
v.extract(ref, schema='vendor:str, total:float, due_date:str')
v.extract_all(doctype='invoice')
```

`decisive=True` means the cues decided without a model.

## Pictures

``` python
v.add_image(path, labels=['Superb Fairywren'])   # metadata is the text; pixels stay on disk
v.add_images(dir)
v.label_images(dir, 'aussie-birds')              # anya classifies, the vault files the result
v.tag_image(ref, labels=[...], caption='...')    # write a later model run onto a picture
v.images(); v.search(q, kind='image')
```

Pictures have `kind='image'`. The searchable text is the filename,
folder, dimensions, camera, capture date and GPS position, with any
labels or caption. `label_images` needs
[anya](https://github.com/vedicreader/anya).

## Code

``` python
v.index_code(dir)                # kosha: AST chunks, symbols, call graph
v.code_search(q); v.symbol(name); v.where_to_add(desc); v.grep(pat, dir)
v.federate(q, dir=dir)           # vault + kosha + ripgrep, fused by rank
```

Once `.kosha/code.db` exists, `context` and `ask` add code sections on
their own.

## Knobs

Retrieval defaults are litesearch’s. Reach for:

- `rerank=True` on `search` / `sections` / `context` when precision
  matters more than latency (needs `vishalakshi[rerank]`)
- `v.shelf(name)` to keep two collections apart, so a large one does not
  crowd a small one out of the rankings
- `llm=` (`auto`, `always` or `never`) for when `categorize` and
  `extract` may ask a model
- `ask(q, pii=)`: default `local` when
  [`local_ok()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#local_ok)
  (the local runtime is importable), else `redact`; never off. The
  result’s `policy` says which ran; a host sets
  `vishalakshi.ask.LOCAL_OK = False` to force `redact`

## Marks and feedback

``` python
v.mark_noisy(doc_id, reason='site furniture')
v.mark_pii(doc_id, reason='address book'); v.mark_not_pii(doc_id, reason='my own invoice')
v.pii(doc_id, ner=True)          # read `scanned_ner`, not the count alone
v.level(doc_id)                  # Open, Personal or Local only; an agent may raise one, never lower it
v.send_check(refs, model=m)      # what a model would get: whole, masked or withheld, and `why`
v.suggest_noisy(k=20); v.accept_noisy(k=10)
v.learn()                        # log every ask as feedback
```

Marks live in `doc_marks` and survive the document being added again.
`suggest_noisy` is 0.988 AUC. Leave `fit_ranker` / `use_ranker` off
unless your corpus says otherwise (`evals/RESULTS.md`).

`connect()`, which needs a model, builds the typed entity graph (LLM
`refers_to`/`defines` edges) and the topic nodes; `graph_search` walks
it, `map` / `topic_tree` read topics. Run `connect()` after a batch of
ingests.

## Watches

``` python
v.watch(url, every='6h')                                   # kind='url': re-read when it changed
v.watch(dir, kind='folder', every='1h', instructions='flag any print()', pattern='*.py')
v.watch('re-read the evals', kind='remind', every='1w')    # one note per reminder
v.watches(); v.poll()                                      # poll drains due work and housekeeps stale documents
```

`kind` is `action` by another name; a `folder` watch fires with `added`,
`changed`, `removed` and its `instructions`, verbatim.

## Notes

`stats` / `sources` / `toc` inspect the vault. Ingest is
content-addressed. Sanskrit turns on vidyut lemmas and Monier-Williams
glosses once.

`forget`, `drop_shelf`, `unwatch` and `pause` are not in `allow`; call
them yourself when you mean to.

This page is a pyskill: a cheat sheet an agent loads with `read_skill`.
The markdown cell above is exported as the module’s docstring, and
`list_pyskills()` reads it without importing the module, taking the
first paragraph as the summary. `allow` registers the vault methods a
sandboxed agent may call, `READ` and `WRITE`: everything that reads the
vault or adds to it. Deleting (`forget`, `drop_shelf`) and stopping
watches (`unwatch`, `pause`) are left out, so an agent cannot do them.
